text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99_decode_latency spiked above 2.5s across us-east-1 GPU pool (gpu-pool-2). Alerts triggered: latency_p95, streaming_stalls > 3s. Auto-notify to #eng-runtime and oncall.

maria (oncall): I'm paged and looking. seeing multiple customer timeouts, some streaming sessions stalled mid-response. Is this correlated with the 20m ago runtime push?

deploy-bot: Deployed runtime:runtime-v2026.03.10-kernel-opt at 2026-03-10T17:15:12Z to gpu-pool-2 (rollout 100%). Change: kernel & compilepath optimizations, TRT 8.7 bump, enable FLASHATTN_OPT flag.

kevin (runtime): yikes. I rolled the kernel/compilepath flags in that build. Noted new flashattn path enabled by default. Repro: local synthetic p99 went up for decode at long sequences.

ashish (sre): Confirming p95+p99 on infra dashboards — p50 unchanged, tail is the problem. Paging looks like paging+tail interactions: decode kernel slower for long-context (>2048). Heap/oom not happening.

maria (oncall): Steps: 1) gather traces (kv cache hit rates, tvm kernel timings) 2) isolate rollout -> can we pin some nodes to previous runtime? 3) mitigation: route traffic off gpu-pool-2 to gpu-pool-1 or enable degraded fallback model.

kevin (runtime): collecting traces now. running `rt-metrics fetch --since 30m --tags kernel,flashattn` and `kubectl get pods -l pool=gpu-pool-2 -o wide`

kevin (runtime): logs show increased latency in decode kernel path -> compilepath spent more time in `kern_conv_fmha` and fallback to slower path for some shapes. Also seeing increase in kernel launch overhead.

jen (eng-oncall): customer-impact: Support dashboard shows 12 active timeouts in last 15m, 3 high-value customers experiencing degraded completions (streaming stalled). SLA breach window about ~6m so far. :grimacing:

emily (pm): flagged in workspace — keeping customers updated. Any ETA on mitigation?

kevin (runtime): quick mitigations I can try now: 1) toggle FLASHATTN_OPT off on runtime (hot flag) 2) rollback runtime to v2026.03.09 which used TRT 8.6 and old compile flags 3) route heavy streaming traffic to dedicated pool with older runtime. Option 1 is least invasive.

maria (oncall): Try option 1 first and observe. If no improvement, do a rollback. Also enable prefix caching aggressively for streaming routes to reduce decode work.

kevin (runtime): toggling flag: `redwood-run ctrl set-feature FLASHATTN_OPT false --pool gpu-pool-2`

kevin (runtime): :hourglass: running...

kevin (runtime): flag flip done. monitoring.

ashish (sre): after flag flip p95 improved from 900ms -> 420ms within two minutes, p99 from 2.9s -> 680ms. streaming stalls dropped. Looks promising. :thumbsup:

maria (oncall): nice. keep it flipped while we root cause. We still need a rollback plan if flip regresses other workloads.

kevin (runtime): collecting perf traces w/ debug symbols and kernel timestamps. Dumping `trt_prof` and `nvprof` traces to s3 path: s3://redwood-debug/1773014500/trace.tar.gz

kevin (runtime): quick note: compilepath change enabled `-Ofast` like aggressive math opts and an experimental kernel generator that picks fmha kernels for shapes under 128x128. That path seems to sometimes cause additional synchronizations on older GPUs -> tail penalties.

tom (mlinfra): We should also check quantization/packing differences. Some kernels assume aligned strides and hit fallback copy paths causing paging. I'll run microbench on same shape.

maria (oncall): customer comms: Jen, Emily, can you confirm list of impacted customers so we prioritize?

jen (eng-oncall): Impacted: acme-ai, payroll-ai, docsummarize-prod (IDs in support dashboard). I sent quick note to acme-ai support that we're mitigating; they'll escalate if they see >10% errors.

emily (pm): keeping them updated. We might schedule a brief engineering status note in 30m to affected accounts.

ashish (sre): for mitigation hardening: 1) we should add autoscale buffer on gpu-pool-1 for overflow routing 2) create transient routing rule to avoid pool-2 until we cap changes 3) temp degrade streaming to non-streaming completions for the heaviest models (tradeoff explicit).

kevin (runtime): I'll open a rollback runbook in case flag flip is insufficient. Command to rollback: `redwood-deploy rollback --service runtime --to v2026.03.09 --pool gpu-pool-2` (requires approvals).

maria (oncall): Approvals: Ashish + Kevin + Eng lead required. Ashish, can you pre-approve if we need it?

ashish (sre): pre-approve if it keeps SLOs. I'll stand by.

kevin (runtime): If we decide to rollback, note that TRT downgrade will impact other optimizations. We'll need smoke tests for correctness and perf. Rolling back also needs to avoid data-plane restarts for active sessions — prefer draining nodes then replace.

kevin (runtime): For root cause tracing: flagged that kernel launch latency increased on Tesla A100 40GB with driver 525.x — maybe new kernels weren't compiled for that driver combination, leading to slower CUDA warmup.

tom (mlinfra): Could be codegen differences for PTX vs SASS. I'll compare PTX diffs and check compile flags: `-maxrregcount`, `-ftz`, `-prec-div` etc.

maria (oncall): Good. For next 30m: keep FLASHATTN_OPT off, monitor, and collect traces. If stable for 20m, we'll keep change and schedule postmortem. If we see new regressions, escalate to rollback.

jen (eng-oncall): noted. Setting incident priority to P2 (customer-impacting, contained).

kevin (runtime): adding an emergency toggle to console to control FLASHATTN_OPT per-pool so we have faster flips in future.

maria (oncall): handoff plan: I'm going off shift in 25m. If still unresolved, next oncall is tom. Tom can you take the handoff if needed?

tom (mlinfra): I got it. I'll take over if still in mitigation. Will continue kernel diffs and run microbench.

maria (oncall): Thanks everyone. Final checklist before handoff: 1) confirm p99 < 1s 2) customer list informed 3) traces uploaded 4) rollback ready if needed.

kevin (runtime): current metrics: p95 420ms, p99 680ms, streaming stalls near baseline. Traces at s3 path uploaded.

jen (eng-oncall): All impacted customers notified. Support queue monitoring.

emily (pm): I'll coordinate postmortem and customer follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated (FLASHATTN_OPT toggled), severity=P2, owners=eng-runtime,mlinfra,sre. Postmortem required if rollback executed or further impact observed.

maria (oncall): Handoff to tom in 10m. If anything spikes, page oncall. Otherwise we'll write up RCA after traces reviewed. :v:

tom (mlinfra): taking notes and will continue in thread. thanks.

(END THREAD)
